claim.claim: Microsoft's net income for fiscal year 2025 increased by more than 10% compared with fiscal year 2024.

verdict.label: SUPPORTED
verdict.reasoning_summary: The claim states that Microsoft's net income for fiscal year 2025 increased by more than 10% compared with fiscal year 2024. Evidence E5, from Microsoft's 10-K filing for the period ending June 30, 2025, shows a comparison table for "Fiscal Year 2025 Compared with Fiscal Year 2024" which explicitly states net income was $101,832 million in FY2025 versus $88,136 million in FY2024, representing a 16% increase. Since 16% > 10%, the claim is supported.

After investigating potential challenges to the initial verdict, none of the hypotheses found supporting evidence:

H1 (Restatements): The retrieved evidence discusses uncertain tax positions and IRS audits but contains no indication that net income figures for fiscal 2024 or 2025 were restated or adjusted after initial reporting.

H2 (One-time items inflating FY2025): The evidence retrieved discusses derivative accounting and general accounting policies but does not identify any extraordinary gains, one-time items, or unusual accounting changes that would have artificially inflated fiscal 2025 net income.

H3 (Non-recurring charges depressing FY2024): Evidence E16 explicitly states "No instances of impairment were identified in our May 1, 2025, May 1, 2024, or May 1, 2023 tests," which refutes the possibility of goodwill impairment charges in fiscal 2024. No evidence of discontinued operations or other significant non-recurring charges in fiscal 2024 was found.

The original evidence (E5) from the 10-K filing clearly shows net income increased from $88,136 million in FY2024 to $101,832 million in FY2025, representing a 16% increase, which exceeds the 10% threshold stated in the claim. This was also confirmed by the numeric check showing a 15.54% year-over-year growth. The challenges found no contradicting evidence, so the verdict remains SUPPORTED.
